rows.label: Current term
rows.value: Sejm of the 10th term, Senate of the 11th

rows.label: Term began
rows.value: 13 November 2023, the Sejm's first sitting. A term starts with the first sitting and runs to the day before the next Sejm's first sitting.

rows.label: Election day
rows.value: Must be a day free from work within the 30 days before the four years run out: 14 October to 12 November 2027. The Sundays in that window are 17, 24 and 31 October and 7 November. Every Sejm election since 1991 has been on a Sunday.

rows.label: Latest date for the order
rows.value: 15 August 2027 (90 days before 13 November). The President's order sets the date and, after the National Electoral Commission's opinion, the electoral calendar; it is published in the Public Information Bulletin and the Journal of Laws within 5 days.

rows.label: First sitting of the new Sejm
rows.value: Convened by the President on a day within 30 days of the election.

rows.label: Court's ruling on validity
rows.value: By the 90th day after the election, by resolution, in the full chamber of the Supreme Court; a protest must be filed within 7 days of the Commission's announcement of the results.

rows.label: Early election
rows.value: The Sejm can shorten its own term by a resolution of at least two thirds of the statutory number of deputies (307 of 460); the President can do so only in cases the Constitution names. The election is then held within 45 days, and the Senate's term is shortened with it.

rows.label: President of the Republic
rows.value: Orders the election by a decree (postanowienie), sets its date, convenes the new Sejm and Senate.

rows.label: National Electoral Commission (PKW)
rows.value: The permanent highest electoral body: supervises compliance with electoral law, appoints the district commissions and electoral commissioners, checks the districts' results and announces the national result in the Journal of Laws. Nine members: one Constitutional Tribunal judge and one Supreme Administrative Court judge, each named by their court's president, and seven people qualified to be judges named by the Sejm.

rows.label: National Electoral Office (KBW)
rows.value: The Commission's secretariat: provides the administrative, financial and technical conditions for the election. Its head is the Commission's secretary and attends with an advisory vote.

rows.label: District electoral commissions
rows.value: One for each of the 41 constituencies: accept candidate lists, count and divide the seats among the lists, and draw up the district's record.

rows.label: Supreme Court
rows.value: Rules on the validity of the election, and of each deputy's election where a protest was filed. Voters may file protests.

rows.label: Marshal of the Sejm
rows.value: Receives the Commission's report on the election with the President and the Supreme Court, within 14 days of the results' announcement.

rows.label: Seats
rows.value: 460 deputies from party lists in multi-member constituencies (41 in 2023). The Senate's 100 are elected at the same time in single-member districts; no one may stand for both houses.

rows.label: Thresholds
rows.value: 5% of valid votes nationally for a party's list, 8% for a coalition's. Lists of registered national-minority organisations are exempt from the 5% (the German Minority in 2023).

rows.label: Allocation
rows.value: D'Hondt within each constituency, among the lists that cleared the threshold; seats go to candidates in order of personal votes.

rows.label: Candidate lists
rows.value: One list per committee in each constituency, filed with the district commission by 16:00 on the 39th day before the election. Each list needs 35% of each sex at least, and no fewer candidates than the constituency has seats and no more than twice as many. A committee with lists in at least half the constituencies need not collect signatures for the rest; otherwise 5,000 voters' signatures per list.

rows.label: Coalitions
rows.value: A party in an electoral coalition may not file lists on its own.
